A-1-X-P.name: Complex Strategic Decision
A-1-X-P.description: Should the company pivot? Should I switch careers? Should the city build a subway?
A-1-X-P.reason: Strategic decisions fear treating symptoms not root causes. Contradiction Analysis finds the real problem (principal contradiction), Strategic Foresight ensures you see beyond the immediate (foresee trends), Systems Thinking prevents tunnel vision (holistic view). All three are indispensable.
steps:
Step 1: List all problems (Contradiction Analysis)
  -> Write down all problems and conflicts you face
  -> Don't filter, write everything

Step 2: Distinguish primary/secondary (Contradiction Analysis)
  -> Which problem pulls one hair and moves the whole body?
  -> Which problem solved makes others auto-relieve?
  -> That's the principal contradiction

Step 3: Draw the big picture (Systems Thinking)
  -> Map the principal contradiction and all related factors as a relationship diagram
  -> Mark which are positive feedback (amplifying), which are negative feedback (suppressing)
  -> Find the leverage points in the system

Step 4: Simulate the future (Strategic Foresight)
  -> If Option A, what happens in 1/3/5 years?
  -> If Option B, what happens in 1/3/5 years?
  -> List best/worst/most likely for each

Step 5: Decide
  -> Choose the option with clearest principal contradiction and most controllable global impact
  -> Make contingency plans
expected: Decisions shift from gut feel to analysis
See 3-5 years ahead
Know what matters, ignore noise
A-1-X-P.case:
A traditional retailer faces e-commerce disruption.
Contradiction Analysis: Surface problem is online stealing business; principal contradiction is offline cannot provide value that online lacks.
Systems Thinking: Offline assets are space+people+immediacy; online assets are data+scale+convenience.
Strategic Foresight: Pure online gets platform-locked, pure offline slowly dies, integration is the way.
Decision: Transform stores to experience centers, online does data-driven recommendations, offline does experience+delivery. In 3 years, offline experience stores become brand moat.

A-1-X-R.name: Long-term Strategic Layout
A-1-X-R.description: Long-term strategic layout, 10-year corporate plan, 10-year personal growth
A-1-X-R.reason: Long-term layout is about survive and thrive. Protracted War Thinking plans three stages (defense->stalemate->counteroffensive), Encircle Cities from Countryside finds niches giants ignore, Gradual Reform ensures progress each stage.
steps:
Step 1: Assess strength (Protracted War)
  -> Honestly assess resource gap vs opponent
  -> If gap >5x, enter defense stage
  -> If gap 2-5x, prepare stalemate
  -> Only if gap <2x, consider counteroffensive

Step 2: Find weak market (Encircle Cities)
  -> Where does opponent serve poorly?
  -> Which customer segments are ignored?
  -> Pick a niche opponent ignores or does badly

Step 3: Build base (Encircle Cities)
  -> Become #1 in that niche
  -> Accumulate reputation, capital, talent
  -> Don't rush to expand, secure the base first

Step 4: Expand gradually (Encircle Cities)
  -> Radiate from base to adjacent markets
  -> Each expansion <=50% of current size
  -> New market must be profitable in 6 months

Step 5: Wait for timing (Protracted War)
  -> When you reach 30-50% of opponent size
  -> Opponent notices you
  -> Enter stalemate: defend + accumulate
  -> Keep deepening your advantage areas

Step 6: Counteroffensive (Protracted War)
  -> When you exceed opponent in a domain
  -> Concentrate resources to attack
  -> One core domain at a time
expected: Foothold in 1 year
Niche advantage in 2-3 years
Capacity to compete head-on with giants in 5 years
A-1-X-R.case:
Pinduoduo rose under Alibaba/JD duopoly.
Encircle Cities: Alibaba/JD focused on tier 1-2 cities, Pinduoduo started from tier 3-4 and rural.
Protracted War: Massive subsidies early, no profit, accumulated users.
Gradual expansion: From agri-products to full category, from sinking market upward.
Result: Became China's 2nd largest e-commerce platform.

A-1-Y-P.name: Business Competition
A-1-Y-P.description: New product launch facing competitors, market share battle, price war
A-1-Y-P.reason: Business competition is not who hits harder, but who thinks smarter. Total Victory Mindset reminds you: best competition is no competition (differentiation), Mental Models help understand competitive landscape from multiple angles, Mobile Warfare says: don't fight every battle, concentrate force on winnable ones.
steps:
Step 1: Know self and enemy (Total Victory)
  -> List your strengths, weaknesses, resources
  -> List competitors' strengths, weaknesses, resources
  -> Find battles opponent must win but you don't need to

Step 2: Multi-angle analysis (Mental Models)
  -> Economics: supply/demand, marginal cost, network effects
  -> Psychology: user decision biases, anchoring
  -> Ecology: species niches, ecological positioning
  -> Military: center of gravity, supply lines, high ground

Step 3: Find your niche (Total Victory)
  -> Where does competitor perform worst?
  -> Can you be best in that market?
  -> If yes, that's your ecological niche

Step 4: Concentrated attack (Mobile Warfare)
  -> All resources on chosen niche
  -> Become absolute #1 in that market
  -> Don't spread thin to other markets

Step 5: Build moat
  -> Brand, network effects, switching costs as barriers
  -> Make it hard for competitors to enter your niche
expected: Avoid head-on price war
Build absolute advantage in niche
Win by differentiation not attrition
A-1-Y-P.case:
A Chinese phone brand vs Apple/Samsung duopoly.
Total Victory: Don't fight on flagships, start with mid-low end.
Mental Models: Network effects (social), anchoring (value), economies of scale.
Mobile Warfare: Concentrate on camera, become best in price segment.
Result: From low-end to high-end breakthrough.

A-1-Y-S.name: Market Research
A-1-Y-S.description: Pre-entry market research, competitor analysis, user personas
A-1-Y-S.reason: Market research fears subjective speculation. Seek Truth from Facts ensures facts over assumptions, Mass Line ensures hearing real user voices not reports, Abstract Induction extracts core patterns from messy data.
steps:
Step 1: Define research goals (Seek Truth)
  -> Clarify 3 core questions
  -> Set time/budget/sample limits

Step 2: Go to frontline (Mass Line)
  -> Shadow support team 3 days, log complaints
  -> Surveys + deep interviews
  -> Don't ask what you like, ask what pains you most

Step 3: Identify core needs
  -> Top 3 mentioned needs
  -> Filter fake needs (say they want but don't use)

Step 4: MVP development (Gradual Reform)
  -> 2 weeks to minimum viable
  -> Budget <=10% of total
  -> Only core-need features

Step 5: Launch + collect data (Feedback Loops)
  -> Positive feedback (more users->more content->more users)
  -> Negative feedback (more users->noise->quality users churn)

Step 6: Continuous iteration
  -> Weekly small releases
  -> Each version incorporates user feedback
expected: Product-market fit improves
Iteration speed 3x faster
Retention significantly higher
A-1-Y-S.case:
A SaaS company wants AI features but doesn't know what.
Flexible Strategy: List 10 AI scenarios (smart support, auto-reports, recommendations).
Gradual Reform: 2 weeks, 3 MVPs, 50 seed users each.
Natural Selection: Smart reports usage 5x others, highest willingness to pay.
Result: Cut other 2, focus on smart reports, core differentiator in 6 months.

A-1-Y-Q.name: Institution Design
A-1-Y-Q.description: Design performance reviews, promotion mechanisms, corporate governance
A-1-Y-Q.reason: Institution design is not just writing rules, but designing a self-regulating system. Procedural Justice ensures fairness, Game Theory designs incentives, Feedback Loops predicts long-term effects.
steps:
Step 1: Clarify institution goal
  -> What problem to solve? (Incentive? Fairness? Efficiency?)

Step 2: Design process (Procedural Justice)
  -> Nomination->Review->Publicity->Appeal, each step has rules

Step 3: Simulate game (Game Theory)
  -> If institution is like this, how will people respond?
  -> Any loopholes to exploit?

Step 4: Predict feedback (Feedback Loops)
  -> What positive feedback will this trigger?
  -> What negative feedback?

Step 5: Pilot in small scope
  -> One department first
  -> 3 months evaluate, adjust, then scale
expected: Institutional fairness significantly improved
Gaming behavior reduced
Employee satisfaction increased
A-1-Y-Q.case:
A company designs new performance review.
Procedural Justice: Nomination->Review->Publicity->Appeal, each step has rules.
Game Theory: Simulate responses, found collusion loophole, added cross-dept review.
Feedback Loops: Predicted short-termism negative feedback, added long-term incentive weight.
Result: Fairness up, gaming down, satisfaction up.

A-2-X-P.name: Investment Decision
A-2-X-P.description: Whether to invest in a project? How to adjust asset allocation?
A-2-X-P.reason: Investments biggest enemy is yourself. Marginal Thinking helps rational allocation (last dollar ROI), Loss Aversion identifies emotional traps, Dual-System Thinking forces rational analysis on big decisions.
steps:
Step 1: Marginal analysis (Marginal Thinking)
  -> Not total return, but marginal return
  -> Where does last dollar earn highest ROI?

Step 2: Identify emotional traps (Loss Aversion)
  -> Refusing to stop loss because already down?
  -> FOMO chasing highs?

Step 3: Forced cooldown (Dual-System)
  -> Any large investment above threshold: 24hr wait
  -> Write decision rationale AND bear case

Step 4: Diversify + Focus
  -> Core (60%) in most certain direction
  -> Satellite (40%) in high-potential directions
expected: Impulsive trades reduced 70%+
Annual return volatility lower
Decision quality from gut to analysis
A-2-X-P.case:
An investor faces add-to-position decision.
Marginal: Where does last 100k earn best?
Loss Aversion: Found self refusing stop-loss due to sunk cost.
Dual-System: 24hr cooldown, wrote bear case.
Result: Avoided chasing high, bought dip on pullback, 15% better annual return.

A-2-Y-P.name: Negotiation
A-2-Y-P.description: Business negotiation, salary negotiation, M&A negotiation
A-2-Y-P.reason: Negotiation is not who hits harder, but who thinks smarter. Total Victory: best competition is no competition (differentiation), Game Theory designs incentives for cooperation.
steps:
Step 1: Know self and counterparty (Total Victory)
  -> List both strengths, weaknesses, resources
  -> Find what they must win but you don't need to

Step 2: Design mechanism (Game Theory)
  -> If negotiation is this way, how will they respond?
  -> How to structure terms so they feel cooperation is optimal?

Step 3: Design BATNA
  -> Your BATNA (best alternative)?
  -> Their BATNA?

Step 4: Concession list
  -> Things you give cheap but they value high
  -> These are your negotiation chips

Step 5: Concession in steps
  -> Don't show all cards at once
  -> Each concession extracts real counter-concession
expected: Avoid passive acceptance of bad terms
Hold ground on core interests
Build long-term partnership not one-off deal
A-2-Y-P.case:
A company renews contract with major client.
Total Victory: Don't fight on price, trade service upgrade for renewal.
Game Theory: Tiered service + incentive rebate, guides client to long-term.
Result: 3-year renewal, price -5% but total value +30%, both satisfied.

A-2-Y-R.name: Long-term Competition (Resources Tight)
A-2-Y-R.description: Startup vs giant, individual in industry, resource-constrained long competition
A-2-Y-R.reason: Resource-tight long competition is about survive and thrive. Encircle Cities finds niches giants ignore, Guerrilla Tactics enables flexible maneuver, Gradual Reform ensures progress each stage.
steps:
Step 1: Assess strength (Protracted War)
  -> Honestly assess resource gap
  -> Gap>5x: defense
  -> Gap 2-5x: stalemate prep
  -> Gap<2x: counteroffensive prep

Step 2: Find weak market (Encircle Cities)
  -> Where does giant serve poorly?
  -> Which customers ignored?
  -> Pick market giant ignores

Step 3: Build base (Encircle Cities)
  -> Become #1 in niche
  -> Accumulate reputation, capital, talent
  -> Don't rush expansion, secure base first

Step 4: Expand gradually (Encircle Cities)
  -> Radiate to adjacent markets
  -> Each expansion <=50% current size
  -> New market profitable in 6 months

Step 5: Wait for timing (Protracted War)
  -> At 30-50% opponent size, enter stalemate
  -> Keep deepening advantage areas

Step 6: Counteroffensive (Protracted War)
  -> When exceeding opponent in a domain
  -> Concentrate resources to attack
  -> One core domain at a time
expected: Foothold in 1 year
Niche advantage in 2-3 years
Head-on capacity vs giants in 5 years
A-2-Y-R.case:
A SaaS startup vs Salesforce monopoly.
Encircle Cities: Salesforce targets enterprise, startup from SMB.
Guerrilla: Free tier early, build user reputation.
Gradual expansion: CRM -> marketing automation, SMB upward.
Result: Vertical #1, acquired by big tech.

A-3-Y-R.name: Breakout from Disadvantage
A-3-Y-R.description: Extremely resource-poor, disadvantaged position, need turnaround
A-3-Y-R.reason: Extreme disadvantage only way out: avoid strength hit weakness, flexible maneuver, self-reliance. Encircle Cities finds gaps opponent ignores, Flexible Strategy adapts fast, Self-Reliance ensures no external bailout dependence.
steps:
Step 1: Admit gap, no head-on
  -> Honestly assess: where absolutely weaker?
  -> Abandon battles you must win but can't

Step 2: Find gaps (Encircle Cities)
  -> Where does opponent serve worst?
  -> Which customers completely ignored?
  -> Pick domain opponent doesn't even care about

Step 3: Flexible maneuver (Flexible Strategy)
  -> No fixed playbook, strike where open
  -> They defend A hard, you attack B
  -> When they react to B, you're already at C

Step 4: Self-reliance (Self-Reliance)
  -> Don't expect external funding/partnership to save
  -> Cash flow must be self-generated
  -> Core tech/capability must be self-developed

Step 5: Accumulate counteroffensive capital
  -> Become #1 in chosen domain
  -> Accumulate cash, talent, tech moats
  -> Wait for opponent mistake or environment shift, then total attack
expected: Foothold in niche in 6 months
Cash flow positive in 1-2 years
Counteroffensive capacity in 3-5 years
A-3-Y-R.case:
Vertical SaaS vs Salesforce.
Admit gap: No full CRM, abandon enterprise.
Find gaps: Focus on medical aesthetics clinic management (Salesforce ignores).
Flexible: Scheduling first, then inventory, then marketing tools.
Self-reliance: Customer prepayments fund ops, no VC.
Result: Vertical #1, reverse entry into general SaaS.

B-2-Y-S.name: Technical Breakthrough
B-2-Y-S.description: Core tech bottleneck, algorithm optimization, architecture refactor
B-2-Y-S.reason: Technical breakthrough is not linear progress, but long accumulation + sudden paradigm shift. Flexible Strategy avoids single-path lock-in, Punctuated Equilibrium reminds breakthroughs come from paradigm shifts, Self-Reliance ensures core tech independence.
steps:
Step 1: Multi-path exploration (Flexible Strategy)
  -> List 3-5 possible technical approaches
  -> Small resource pre-research each
  -> Don't put all eggs in one basket

Step 2: Spot paradigm shift (Punctuated Equilibrium)
  -> Watch new papers, frameworks, hardware
  -> Ask: any new paradigm makes old problem simple?
  -> e.g., Transformer made NLP from RNN obsolete

Step 3: Core self-reliance (Self-Reliance)
  -> Core algorithms/arch must be self-developed
  -> Key dependencies must have fallbacks
  -> Cannot be locked by single vendor/opensource

Step 4: Small fast validation
  -> Minimum prototype each direction
  -> Benchmarks speak, not intuition

Step 5: Focused breakthrough
  -> Resources to most promising 1 path
  -> Concentrate firepower on core challenge
expected: Avoid 6+ months wasted on wrong direction
Core tech self-controlled
Breakthrough speed 2-3x
B-2-Y-S.case:
An AI chip company cracks sparse compute acceleration.
Multi-path: Sparse matrix compression, dynamic pruning, knowledge distillation 3 paths.
Punctuated Equilibrium: Found sparse patterns auto-optimizable by compiler (paradigm shift).
Self-reliance: Core compiler self-built, not dependent on TVM/MLIR upstream.
Result: 60% latency reduction, 3x energy efficiency.

B-1-Z-S.name: Product Rapid Iteration
B-1-Z-S.description: Zero-to-one product, MVP validation, PMF search
B-1-Z-S.reason: Products aren't built in isolation. Flexible Strategy responds fast to market feedback, Feedback Loops builds growth flywheel, Gradual Reform iterates in small steps.
steps:
Step 1: Rapid hypotheses (Flexible Strategy)
  -> 5 core hypotheses (user needs X, pays Y, channel Z)
  -> Sort by validation cost, test cheapest first

Step 2: MVP (Gradual Reform)
  -> 2 weeks to minimum viable
  -> Budget <=10% total
  -> No admin backend, core interaction first

Step 3: Real user test (Feedback Loops)
  -> 20 seed users try
  -> Positive feedback (more users->more value->more users)
  -> Negative feedback (more users->worse exp->churn)

Step 4: Data-driven iteration
  -> Weekly release
  -> Each version changes 1-2 KPI features
  -> A/B test every change

Step 5: Build growth flywheel
  -> Identify loop (acquire->activate->retain->refer->acquire)
  -> Strengthen positive, cut negative
  -> Dashboard with daily north-star metric
expected: MVP live in 2 weeks
PMF validated in 1 month
Iteration speed 3x
B-1-Z-S.case:
Team building AI writing tool.
Rapid hypotheses: Users need outline generation not full text.
MVP: 2 weeks outline generator, 50 seed users.
Feedback Loops: Users love outline->fulltext one-click, 40% retention.
Rapid iteration: 1 template/week, 10k DAU in 3 months.

C-2-Y-P.name: Leadership Development
C-2-Y-P.description: IC to leader transition, new manager adaptation
C-2-Y-P.reason: Good leaders don't manage everything, they manage the right things. Mass Line ensures hearing truth, Wu Wei teaches letting go, Systems Thinking sees org holistically.
steps:
Step 1: Go to frontline (Mass Line)
  -> Half day/week with team
  -> Don't ask what's the problem, ask what blocks you
  -> Log: what makes them feel powerless, waste time, lack support

Step 2: Set goals and standards (Wu Wei)
  -> Only set goals/standards, don't dictate how
  -> Let team find their way
  -> Your job: remove obstacles, not direct moves

Step 3: Draw org map (Systems Thinking)
  -> Mark key roles, dependencies, info flows
  -> Find single points of failure (person leaves = system down)

Step 4: Rotation system
  -> Team members rotate as Tech Lead
  -> Grow next-gen leaders
  -> You gradually exit daily decisions
expected: Team autonomy increases
Leader freed from daily approvals
Org resilience strengthened
C-2-Y-P.case:
Tech director from IC to management.
Frontline: Half day/week code review + sit in meetings, ask what blocks not progress.
Wu Wei: Only set deliver X feature + 80% coverage, no tech direction.
Systems: Drew architecture deps, found auth service as single point, drove refactor.
Result: Team autonomous delivery up, he got time for strategy.

C-2-Z-P.name: Conflict Mediation
C-2-Z-P.description: Team internal conflicts, cross-dept friction, partner disputes
C-2-Z-P.reason: Conflict essence is unmet needs collision. Contradiction Analysis sees through phenomenon to essence, Framing Effect reframes to reduce antagonism, United Front redirects to shared goals.
steps:
Step 1: Separate private talks (Seek Truth)
  -> Talk to each party alone, no stance
  -> Ask: Core demand? Absolute bottom line?
  -> Log both core interests, red lines, emotional triggers

Step 2: Reframe (Framing Effect)
  -> Not who right/wrong, but what shared goal blocked?
  -> A vs B wrong -> we both want success, methods differ
  -> Zero-sum -> positive-sum

Step 3: Open dialogue (Contradiction Analysis)
  -> Face to face, you facilitate
  -> Each says: I understand their demand is...
  -> Find principal contradiction (usually 1 core disagreement)

Step 4: Third option (United Front)
  -> Not A compromise or B compromise, but 3rd way
  -> Find common enemy (competitor/deadline/tech debt)
  -> Turn internal conflict into external shared challenge

Step 5: Written agreement
  -> Who does what, deadline, breach handling
  -> Set review checkpoint (2 weeks)
expected: 1-2 sessions resolve most cooperation conflicts
Culture: conflicts can be constructive
Avoid talent loss, project delays
C-2-Z-P.case:
R&D vs Product over frequent requirement changes.
Contradiction: Core issue not many changes, but zero-cost changes.
Reframe: Who right/wrong -> how to make changes orderly.
United Front: Common enemy is delivery delay.
Agreement: Changes need PO sign-off + impact assessment, emergency fast-track with post-fix.
Result: Change throughput 3x, no more antagonism.

C-3-Y-S.name: Interpersonal Relations
C-3-Y-S.description: Workplace conflicts, managing up, cross-dept collaboration
C-3-Y-S.reason: 90% interpersonal issues stem from cognitive biases and framing misalignment. Cognitive Bias Identification reveals blind spots, Framing Effect changes response by changing expression, Dual-System reminds slow thinking before key conversations.
steps:
Step 1: Identify own biases (Cognitive Bias ID)
  -> Interpreting no reply as disrespect? (confirmation bias)
  -> Feeling owed because I gave much? (sunk cost)
  -> Write: how much of my judgment is fact vs inference?

Step 2: Reframe communication (Framing Effect)
  -> Not you always..., but when X happened I felt Y, I hope Z
  -> Accusation -> request, accusation -> shared goal
  -> E.g., you don't support me -> this project matters, I need specific support...

Step 3: Activate slow thinking (Dual-System)
  -> 10 min forced wait before important convo
  -> Write: my goal? their need?
  -> Rehearse: if they refuse, how I respond?

Step 4: Seek win-win
  -> Ask: what outcome good for both?
  -> Propose specific, low-cost, acceptable action
  -> Set review checkpoint
expected: Conflict escalation probability down 80%
Cross-dept collaboration significantly improved
Reusable communication templates established
C-3-Y-S.case:
PM vs designer over design delivery delay.
Bias ID: PM thought designer procrastinating, actually waiting upstream requirements.
Reframe: Why so slow -> we launch Friday, need lock Wednesday, what support you need?
Dual-System: PM cools 10 min, realizes anxiety projection.
Result: Designer delivered Wednesday, project on time.

D-1-Y-R.name: Personal Growth Planning
D-1-Y-R.description: Career planning, skill tree building, side hustle choice, lifelong learning
D-1-Y-R.reason: Personal growth is a marathon. Gradual Reform avoids overcommitment, Mental Models builds cross-domain framework, Natural Selection: try many, fail fast, keep what fits.
steps:
Step 1: Inventory current state (Seek Truth)
  -> Skill matrix: list skills, rate 1-10
  -> Time audit: where did last week go?
  -> Energy audit: what charges vs drains you?

Step 2: Build skill tree (Mental Models)
  -> Core skill (moat): 1 to top 10%
  -> Satellite skills (leverage): 3-5 at standard
  -> New domain exploration: 1 per quarter

Step 3: Small fast steps (Gradual Reform)
  -> Weekly micro-goal (read 1 chapter, write 1 article, practice 1 hr)
  -> Not perfection, done
  -> Retro: what learned this week? what change next?

Step 4: Natural Selection (Natural Selection)
  -> Quarterly review: what compounds? what depreciates?
  -> Keep compounding skills (writing, coding, English, investment thinking)
  -> Cut depreciating/no-feedback investments

Step 5: Build compounding system
  -> Input: 30 min/day high-quality
  -> Process: Feynman/zettelkasten/mindmap
  -> Output: 1 article/week or code
  -> Feedback: collect -> adjust input
expected: Clear skill radar in 1 year
Expert moat in 1 domain in 3 years
Sustainable lifelong learning system built
D-1-Y-R.case:
Programmer wants to pivot to AI.
Inventory: Coding strong, math weak, English average.
Skill tree: Core=Python+DL frameworks, Satellite=math+paper reading.
Gradual: 1hr/day papers+replication, weekend blog retros.
Natural Selection: 3 months quit RL (poor feedback), focus CV.
Result: Top conference paper in 1 year, pivot successful.

D-2-Y-R.name: Organizational Capability Building
D-2-Y-R.description: Engineering systems, R&D processes, talent pipeline
D-2-Y-R.reason: Org capability building is a protracted war. Protracted War stages it (foundation->system->results), Encircle Cities starts from strongest pain point, Gradual Reform ensures each step solid.
steps:
Step 1: Assess current (Protracted War)
  -> Honest eval: eng efficiency, code quality, delivery cycle, talent density
  -> If foundation very weak: defense (stop bleeding)
  -> If foundation okay: stalemate (build system)
  -> If foundation good: counteroffensive (benchmark)

Step 2: Find entry point (Encircle Cities)
  -> Which dept has strongest pain, strongest will, least resistance?
  -> Pick 1 dept as pilot, don't roll out all
  -> E.g., CI/CD in core business team first, then company-wide

Step 3: Build base (Encircle Cities)
  -> Pilot team runs: process, tools, standards, metrics
  -> Output: templates, automated pipelines, quality gates
  -> Verify: delivery faster, defects down, satisfaction up

Step 4: Expand gradually (Encircle Cities)
  -> Radiate from pilot to adjacent teams
  -> Each expansion <=50% current size
  -> New team must run process in 3 months

Step 5: Stalemate and counteroffensive (Protracted War)
  -> At 50% coverage: consolidate + optimize
  -> At 80%+: publish standards, enable others, build brand
expected: Core team runs eng system in 6 months
60%+ teams covered in 1 year
Industry-benchmarkable eng effectiveness in 2 years
D-2-Y-R.case:
Mid-size tech builds eng system.
Protracted War: Don't talk standards first, solve 2hr build pain.
Encircle Cities: Core transaction team pilot, CI/CD to 15min.
Gradual Reform: Pipeline first, then code standards, test coverage gates.
Gradual expansion: 1 team -> 3 teams -> 12 teams.
Counteroffensive: Published Engineering Effectiveness Whitepaper, industry benchmark.

D-2-Z-P.name: Crisis Response
D-2-Z-P.description: Major outage, PR crisis, key personnel loss
D-2-Z-P.reason: Crisis moments, Contradiction Analysis finds primary/secondary, Seek Truth forces facing truth, Redundancy Backup is last defense.
steps:
Step 1: Classify severity (Contradiction Analysis)
  -> Is this P0 (fatal), P1 (severe), P2 (general)?
  -> What is principal contradiction? Secondary?
  -> Who is decision maker? Executor? Informed?

Step 2: Stop bleeding (Seek Truth)
  -> Admit problem, no cover-up, no blame-shifting
  -> Take most direct stop-loss action
  -> E.g., outage->cut traffic/degrade/rollback; PR->apologize/publish facts/rectify

Step 3: Activate backup (Redundancy Backup)
  -> Critical paths have Plan B?
  -> Key person has backup?
  -> Data/service has geo-redundancy?

Step 4: Root cause retrospective
  -> 5 whys, dig to systemic root cause
  -> Distinguish: technical, process, management, culture causes
  -> Create action items: owner, deadline, acceptance criteria

Step 5: Institutionalize
  -> Turn lessons into norms/tools/processes
  -> Drill: regular fault drills/crisis simulations
  -> Retro: next time same issue caught and stopped in minutes?
expected: P0 outage recovery <30 minutes
PR crisis 24hr turnaround
Same issue zero recurrence
D-2-Z-P.case:
An e-commerce big promo core transaction chain outage 15 min.
Contradiction: Principal contradiction is DB master write block, secondary is cache penetration.
Seek Truth: Admit outage, cut read-only mode stop loss, public apology.
Redundancy: Replica promoted to master, geo-backup restored data.
Root cause: Promo pre-heat script unrate-limited caused write storm.
Institutionalize: Pre-promo mandatory stress test, rate limit, circuit breaker trio.
Result: Next year promo zero outage, fault drill routine established.

D-3-Z-P.name: Survival Crisis
D-3-Z-P.description: Company near bankruptcy, project about to be cut, personal job loss/major illness
D-3-Z-P.reason: Survival moments tolerate zero fakes and delays. Seek Truth forces facing brutal reality, Contradiction Analysis finds the one lifeline in chaos, Redundancy Backup is last lifeline - critical paths must have alternatives.
steps:
Step 1: Face reality (Seek Truth)
  -> Stop all sugarcoating, delays, wishful thinking
  -> Write: how many months cash runway? core business survival?
  -> List all debts, commitments, hard costs

Step 2: Find the one lifeline (Contradiction Analysis)
  -> List all problems, find only the if-unsolved-tomorrow-we-die one
  -> Everything else paused, all hands on this one
  -> E.g., cash flow break is principal contradiction, strategy/culture/brand all yield

Step 3: Configure redundancy (Redundancy Backup)
  -> Critical paths must have Plan B, Plan C
  -> Cash: min 3 months operating reserve
  -> Key talent: critical roles must have backups
  -> Core business: must have degradation mode (e.g., manual/read-only fallback)

Step 4: Extreme focus execution
  -> Everyone only does survival-relevant work
  -> Daily standup: what did for survival yesterday? what today?

B-1-Y-S.name: Innovation Breakthrough
B-1-Y-S.description: Tech innovation, business model innovation, disruptive innovation
B-1-Y-S.reason: Innovation is not linear, but mutation. Natural Selection reminds: many trials, fast iterations, keep what fits. Punctuated Equilibrium tells: breakthroughs often from paradigm shifts. Flexible Strategy lets you not dead-end on single path.
steps:
Step 1: Multi-path exploration (Natural Selection)
  -> Simultaneously try 3-5 different tech/business paths
  -> Each path small resource, clear stop-loss
  -> Don't put all eggs in one basket

Step 2: Spot paradigm shift (Punctuated Equilibrium)
  -> Watch: any new theory, tool, infrastructure emerging?
  -> Ask: can this change make previously "impossible" become "possible"?
  -> e.g., Transformer made NLP from RNN obsolete

Step 3: Rapid validation and screening (Flexible Strategy)
  -> Each path does minimum viability validation (MVP/prototype/experiment)
  -> Data speaks, not intuition
  -> Stop-loss: underperforming paths decisively cut

Step 4: Focused breakthrough
  -> Resources concentrate on most promising 1 path
  -> Concentrate firepower on core challenge
  -> Build tech/commercial moat

Step 5: Scale up
  -> On validated basis, rapid expansion
  -> Standardize, automate, platformize
  -> Form new growth curve
expected: Avoid 6+ months wasted on wrong direction
Establish multi-path exploration mechanism
Breakthrough speed 2-3x
B-1-Y-S.case:
A company wants to do AI drug discovery.
Natural Selection: Simultaneously explore molecule generation, protein folding, virtual screening 3 paths.
Punctuated Equilibrium: AlphaFold2 released, protein folding solved (paradigm shift).
Flexible Strategy: Decisively cut protein folding self-dev, leverage AlphaFold2 for downstream apps.
Focus breakthrough: Concentrate resources on molecule generation challenge.
Result: 6 months launched first candidate drug, entered pre-clinical.

C-1-Y-P.name: Team Building
C-1-Y-P.description: Forming new team, team integration, culture shaping
C-1-Y-P.reason: Team isn't ready just by hiring. Mass Line ensures hearing real voices, United Front helps integrate differences, Management by Objectives aligns everyone to goals.
steps:
Step 1: Deep understanding (Mass Line)
  -> 1-on-1 deep interviews each member
  -> Ask: what you excel at? want to do? worry about?
  -> Log: skill matrix, willingness matrix, concerns list

Step 2: Find consensus (United Front)
  -> Identify core values overlap
  -> Find "greatest common divisor" as team culture foundation
  -> Allow differences, but core must align

Step 3: Set goals (Management by Objectives)
  -> Jointly create OKRs, not top-down decomposition
  -> Goals challenging but achievable
  -> Establish weekly/monthly/quarterly review rhythm

Step 4: Establish mechanisms
  -> Weekly: sync progress, expose problems, mutual help
  -> Retro: victory retro, failure retro, all retro
  -> Feedback: timely, specific, actionable

Step 5: Continuous iteration
  -> Quarterly review: culture healthy? goals aligned?
  -> Adjust: people, process, incentives
  -> New member onboarding: culture package
expected: Team cohesion significantly improved
Goal alignment >90%
Per capita output up 30%+
C-1-Y-P.case:
A startup core team expanded from 5 to 20.
Mass Line: Founder 1-on-1 each, found "tech debt" biggest pain.
United Front: Established "User value first, Tech excellence, Radical transparency" three values.
MBO: All participate in quarterly OKRs, weekly public progress.
Result: 6 months delivered 3 core versions, zero major incidents, team satisfaction 4.8/5.

H-HZX-001.name: 黄宗羲
H-HZX-001.description_en: 黄宗羲（1610-1695），字太冲，号梨洲，浙江余姚人，明末清初三大思想家之一（与顾炎武、王夫之并称）。其父黄尊素为东林党人，阉党害死，宗羲青年时持金棍讼冤庭前，击毙缇骑一人，后长期组织抗清斗争。明亡后终身不仕清朝，著书讲学于浙江甬上。他在政治哲学上提出'天下为主，君为客'的激进民本思想，批判专制君主制为'天下之大害'；在学术史上首创学案体例，以'一本万殊'为指导思想编纂《明儒学案》，开创中国学术史研究传统；在哲学上坚持理气一元论，反对程朱'理在气先'；在史学方法论上强调'经世应务'与'实事求是'并重。其思想对清代浙东学派、晚清维新运动（梁启超称《明夷待访录》为'刺激民族觉醒之最伟大作品'）
H-HZX-001.reason_en: Huang Zongxi (1610-1695) was a Ming-Qing dynasty thinker whose 10 thinking modes cover political philosophy, institutional design, epistemology and core domains
